title: What do plant roots do?
answer: A plant’s roots reach into soil or another place where the plant grows. They help hold the plant steady when wind pushes on the leaves. Many roots also soak up water and minerals. The plant moves those supplies to other parts, including new shoots. A carrot has a thick main root that stores food. Grass often has a spreading bunch of thinner roots. A plant can have important parts below the ground even when you only see leaves above it.
facts: Many roots have tiny root hairs that help take in water.

title: Why do plants have stems?
answer: A stem holds plant parts in places where they can do their jobs. A tall stem can lift leaves toward the light. It can also raise flowers where insects or wind can reach them. Inside many stems, tiny passageways carry water and sugars. Stems can be soft, like the stem of a bean plant, or hard and woody, like a tree trunk. Some run sideways instead of growing up. Others are hidden underground and store food.
facts: A tree trunk is a type of stem.

title: How do leaves help a plant grow?
answer: Leaves give many plants a wide surface to catch sunlight. A green leaf uses light, water and a gas from the air to make sugars. That process is called photosynthesis. The lines you see on many leaves are veins. They bring water in and help move sugars where the plant can use them. Leaves also have tiny openings, often on the lower side. Gases and water vapor can move through those openings even when the leaf looks still.
facts: Some plants have leaves divided into little parts called leaflets.

title: How does water reach the top of a tree?
answer: When water leaves a tree’s leaves as vapor, it helps pull more water upward. Water molecules tend to cling to one another. This lets the pull travel down columns of water inside tiny tubes. The tubes are part of a water-carrying tissue called xylem. Water from the soil enters the roots and helps refill those columns. The whole path can reach from the fine tips of roots to leaves at the very top of a tree.
facts: Water can travel through a path of connected xylem cells.

title: How does a plant send sugar to its roots?
answer: A leaf might make more sugar than it needs right away. The plant can send some of that sugar to other places through a tissue called phloem. A growing root or fruit might use the sugar, or a plant part might store it. The direction depends on where sugars are ready to move and where they are needed. Later, sugar released from a storage part can travel to a new shoot, even before that shoot has many leaves.
facts: Growing roots and fruits can receive sugars through phloem.

title: Why do plants release water vapor?
answer: Water from damp cells inside a leaf can turn into vapor. That vapor escapes through small openings called stomata. The process is called transpiration. Humid air already holds a lot of water vapor, so the loss is often slower in humid air than in dry air. A steady loss of water through leaves helps move more water up through the plant. If water is scarce, closing the openings can slow the loss and help the plant hold on to water.
facts: Plants can change how wide their stomata open.

title: What is inside a flower?
answer: Colorful petals are the most obvious parts of many flowers. Look closer and you may see small structures that make pollen or collect it. In many flowers, the pollen makers are called stamens. A sticky surface called a stigma can catch grains of pollen. Below it, part of the flower can grow into a fruit with seeds. Some kinds of flowers have all these parts together. Other kinds put pollen-making and seed-making parts in different flowers.
facts: The stamens are the pollen-making parts of many flowers.

title: Why is a tomato a fruit?
answer: In a tomato flower, a small part where seeds can develop, called the ovary grows into the tomato. That makes a tomato a fruit in botany, the study of plants. It has seeds inside, just as a peach or a grape does. A cucumber and a pea pod count as fruits for the same reason. People who cook often group these foods with vegetables because of how they taste and how we use them. Both groupings can be useful.
aliases: is a tomato a fruit or vegetable
facts: Peas grow inside pods, which are fruits in botany.

title: How does a seed wake up and grow?
answer: A dry seed can hold a tiny plant and its food supply for a long time. When conditions fit what that kind of plant needs, the seed takes in water and swells. A little root often breaks through the seed coat first. A shoot can then grow in another direction and reach the light. Early on, the young plant uses food stored in the seed. After green leaves open, the plant can make more of its own sugar.
facts: For many kinds of seeds, the root begins growing before the shoot.

title: How do seeds get far from the parent plant?
answer: A seed often has a better chance to find space and light if it lands away from its parent. A dandelion makes tiny dry fruits that float in the breeze on little parachutes. A burr can hitch a ride by hooking onto fur or a sock. Other plants hide seeds inside sweet fruit. An animal can eat the fruit, go somewhere else and leave some seeds behind. Some seeds also travel by floating in water or rolling down a slope.
facts: The little parachute on a dandelion helps the fruit carry its seed in the wind.

title: What is hidden inside a tulip bulb?
answer: A tulip bulb packs together a short stem, a new bud and thick layers that hold food. Most of this rests underground when the plant has no green top. When conditions are right, a shoot can rise and use that stored food. Roots can grow from the small hard base. An onion is another kind of bulb. Its fleshy rings are easier to see than the tightly packed layers of a tulip bulb, but their storage job is much the same.
aliases: how onion and tulip bulbs work
facts: An onion’s thick layers are mostly storage leaves.

title: What are the eyes on a potato?
answer: The eyes on a potato are places where buds can grow. Each bud can start a shoot if the potato has suitable conditions. A potato is a tuber, a thick storage part that develops on an underground stem. It holds food the plant made earlier. Because it is a stem part, a potato can make new shoots at several points. The thick part of a sweet potato may look similar from the outside, but it is a storage root.
facts: A sweet potato and a regular potato store food in different parts of the plant.

title: How does a plant spread by underground stems?
answer: A rhizome is a stem that grows sideways, often just below the ground. Roots can grow down from it. New leafy shoots can grow up at points along the stem. That is one way irises fill more space over time. The old and new shoots can stay connected through the rhizome even when only their tops are visible. A rhizome can also store food, giving a new shoot a supply before it grows enough leaves to make its own.
aliases: what kind of plant part is ginger
facts: The part of a ginger plant sold as “ginger root” is actually a rhizome.

title: How does a strawberry plant make a runner?
answer: A strawberry plant can stretch a long, thin stem across the soil. The stem is called a runner. At places along it, a little copy of the plant can grow leaves and reach down with new roots. At first the tiny plant is joined to the older one. Once its roots and leaves can do enough work, it can survive on its own. This lets one strawberry plant make several nearby plants even in a season when it makes few seeds.
aliases: little strawberry plants on a stem
facts: A stem that runs along the ground to make new plants can also be called a stolon.

title: Why do leaves change color in fall?
answer: A summer maple leaf looks green because it has a lot of a substance called chlorophyll. In fall, as days get shorter, the leaf makes less chlorophyll and the green color fades. Other colors that were harder to see can now show through. They include some yellow and orange colors. Some leaves make additional red or purple coloring in fall. Different kinds of trees can turn different colors, and light and temperature can help change how bright the colors look.
facts: Yellow or orange colors can already be present before a green leaf changes color.

title: How do evergreen trees stay green all year?
answer: Evergreen plants keep some green leaves throughout the year. That does not mean that each leaf lasts forever. An evergreen tree can shed older leaves as it grows replacements, rather than dropping most leaves at once. Many pines and spruces have narrow needles with a coating that helps limit water loss. Some other evergreens have wide, flat leaves. The trick is keeping living leaves through winter or a dry season, whatever shape those leaves happen to be.
facts: Some plants with broad, flat leaves are evergreen too.

title: What are pine cones for?
answer: Pine trees make cones as part of making seeds. Small pollen cones release pollen into the air. A larger seed cone has scales, the stiff plates you can see on a pine cone. Seeds grow where they are protected by those scales. In some species, a cone opens when it dries, and the seeds can fall or blow away. A pine tree does not make a fruit around its seeds, which is one way it differs from a tomato plant.
facts: A pine has small pollen cones as well as larger seed cones.

title: How can moss grow without true roots?
answer: Mosses are small plants that often make soft green mats. Instead of true roots, many have tiny threads that hold the plant in place. Moisture can reach much of a moss plant right through the outside. You may find moss where the ground or a rock stays damp, though some kinds can dry out and start growing again when wet. Moss can spread using spores. These may leave a little case that stands above the green mat.
facts: A moss can grow a spore case at the tip of a slender stalk.

title: Why do some ferns have dots under their leaves?
answer: Turn over a mature leaf on some ferns and you may see rows of round brown spots. The spots are groups of tiny cases that hold spores. When spores are ready, those cases release them, and air can carry them away. In a suitable place, a spore can start a small separate stage of the fern’s life. Later a new leafy fern can grow. Ferns have roots, stems and leaves, yet they make no flowers or seeds.
facts: A fern leaf is also called a frond.

title: How big can a giant sequoia get?
answer: A giant sequoia builds a trunk wide enough to make people standing beside it look tiny. It is famous for the amount of wood in that trunk. The General Sherman Tree is the largest known living single-stem tree by trunk volume. A few other kinds of trees grow taller, but they do not have trunks with as much wood. Wild giant sequoias grow in groves on the western side of California’s Sierra Nevada. Their seeds are much smaller than the huge trees they can become.
facts: The General Sherman Tree is a giant sequoia in Sequoia National Park.

title: Why are coast redwoods famous?
answer: Coast redwoods are the tallest living trees known. They grow naturally along a narrow stretch of the Pacific coast in California and a small part of Oregon. Winter rain and summer fog help keep their forests moist. A redwood may rise far above the plants at its foot, yet its cones are fairly small. A redwood’s height tells you one thing about its size. A giant sequoia’s wider trunk often contains more wood even when the giant sequoia is shorter.
facts: Coast redwood and giant sequoia are two different kinds of trees.

title: How does a Venus flytrap catch a fly?
answer: A Venus flytrap has hinged leaves with tiny hairs on their inside surfaces. When a small insect moves around and brushes the right hairs within a short time, a leaf can snap closed. The plant can get helpful nutrients from the trapped animal. It lives in places where some nutrients are hard to get from the ground. Its green parts still use sunlight to make sugars, as the leaves of other green plants do. Catching animals helps the plant meet a different need.
facts: Wild Venus flytraps are native to a small part of North and South Carolina.

title: How does a pitcher plant catch insects?
answer: Some pitcher plants make hollow leaves shaped like deep cups. An insect can slip inside and find it hard to climb out. The plant gains nutrients as the captured food breaks down. In a purple pitcher plant, rain can collect in the leaf and tiny living things may help break down the material inside. This can help a plant in a wet place where its roots cannot find a large supply of certain nutrients. The pitcher is a special kind of leaf.
facts: Some pitcher plants have leaves that collect rainwater.

title: What part of a fungus is a mushroom?
answer: A mushroom can be the visible part of a fungus that makes and releases spores. Much of the same fungus may be growing as fine threads in soil, leaves or wood. Those hidden threads collect food and can keep growing even when no mushroom is in sight. A mushroom pushes some of the fungus above the material where it lives. That can give its tiny spores a better chance of reaching the air and traveling to another spot.
facts: Many mushroom species have gills or pores where spores form.

title: Where is most of a fungus hiding?
answer: A fungus often grows as a net of tiny branching threads. The whole net is called mycelium. A branch can grow along the inside of a fallen stick or weave through spaces between pieces of soil. The threads can take in food after the fungus releases substances that break larger materials into smaller pieces. If a fungus makes a mushroom, the threads may stay in place after the mushroom dries out. Then a new mushroom can appear later.
facts: Many fungi have threads too thin to see well without a microscope.

title: How do fungi help a fallen log break down?
answer: A fallen branch still has food materials locked inside its tough wood. Some fungi grow into the branch and release substances that break the wood down. They absorb some of the smaller pieces for food. In time, the wood can become soft or crumble. Some of its materials return to the soil or air in other forms. This work makes fungi important decomposers. A forest can keep using materials from old growth even as living trees add whole new branches and leaves.
facts: Not all fungi take apart wood in the same way.

title: Why can lichens grow on bare rocks?
answer: A lichen grows when a fungus lives closely with a partner that can make sugars using light. That partner can be a kind of alga or a kind of tiny living thing called a cyanobacterium. The fungus makes most of the sheltering body you see. Its partner helps supply food. Together they can grow on surfaces like rock, wood or tree bark. A lichen does not need to have plant roots reaching down into a pocket of soil.
facts: Lichens can have shapes like thin crusts, flat leaves or tiny branches.

title: How can a fungus help a plant root?
answer: Some fungi grow right against plant roots or inside parts of the roots. Their thin threads can reach more ground than the root could cover by itself. The fungus can pass useful minerals or water to the plant. The plant can share some of the food materials it makes using sunlight. This partnership is called a mycorrhiza. If you look at a whole tree from above ground, you may never notice the many tiny partnerships helping it below the surface.
facts: A plant and its fungal partners can share materials in both directions.

title: What happens to old leaves in the soil?
answer: A leaf that falls into soil can become food for little animals, fungi and other living things. They break it into smaller parts. Some of those materials stay in the soil in changed forms. Together with pieces of roots and other once-living things, they are part of the soil’s organic matter. This material can help soil hold water and make nutrients available to plants. A fresh leaf and a bit of dark older soil can belong to the same long recycling process.
facts: Some organic matter stays mixed into soil much longer than a fresh leaf lasts.

title: Why do some soils feel gritty or sticky?
answer: Soil contains mineral pieces of different sizes. Sand has the largest of the three common groups, so it often feels gritty. Silt is finer. Clay pieces are so small that wet clay-rich soil can feel sticky and smooth. Most soils have a mix of these sizes. The mix is called soil texture. It helps affect how fast water can move and how much stays between particles. The texture of a garden patch can differ from soil only a short walk away.
facts: Soil texture depends on the mix of sand, silt and clay particles.

title: What makes something a mixture?
answer: A bowl with rice and beans holds a mixture. You can add more of either food and still recognize the pieces. Mixtures can be harder to see, too. Salt may spread out in water until both parts look like one clear liquid. The amount of salt can change from one glass to another. With a pure substance like water, molecules of that substance always have the same set of atoms. Some mixtures look even all the way through. Others have parts you can see.

title: Where does sugar go when it dissolves?
answer: When sugar dissolves, it is still there even after you stop seeing the grains. Water separates the sugar molecules from the grain and surrounds them without breaking apart the individual molecules. The tiny sugar molecules spread throughout the water, making an even mixture called a solution. Stirring moves less sugary water toward the grains and carries sugar away from them. If you let the water leave as vapor, some of the dissolved material can collect as solid again. Dissolving sugar is different from changing it into another substance.
facts: Stirring can help sugar dissolve faster.

title: Why does extra sugar stay on the bottom?
answer: At a given temperature, a glass of water can hold only a certain amount of dissolved sugar. When it holds as much as it can, the solution is saturated. Extra sugar can remain as grains at the bottom even after plenty of stirring. Warming water often lets it hold more sugar, though not every substance responds to temperature in the same way. When a concentrated sugar solution cools, it may no longer be able to hold all that sugar in the water.

facts: A saturated solution can still look clear above any extra solid.

title: How is a compound different from a mixture?
answer: A compound forms when atoms of different elements join in a fixed pattern or proportion. Water is a compound. Each water molecule contains two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom. Mixing extra salt into water does not give a water molecule an extra atom. It makes a mixture with different kinds of particles sharing the same space. Some compounds, such as water, come in separate molecules. Others, such as ordinary table salt, can make repeating patterns with no single molecule to separate out.

facts: In each water molecule, two hydrogen atoms are joined to one oxygen atom.

title: Why do crystals have neat shapes?
answer: In a crystal, very small particles fit together in a pattern that repeats. Adding more particles in matching positions can grow that same pattern outward. The resulting solid may have flat faces or sharp edges that reflect its inner arrangement. Some salt grains look like tiny boxes when you see them through a magnifier. A broken crystal may have chipped or uneven edges, but its remaining particles still follow a pattern. Crystals can grow from melted, dissolved or gaseous materials in suitable conditions.
facts: Even a crystal too small to study with your eyes has a repeating arrangement inside.

title: Why don’t oil and water mix evenly?
answer: In water, the parts of each molecule that pull on nearby molecules help water gather together. Oil molecules do not make the same strong connections with water. If you shake oil and water, some oil breaks into little drops, but the drops can bump into one another and join up again. Many cooking oils also have lower density than water, so their layer ends up on top. Floating and failing to dissolve are different effects. Both can happen in the same glass.

title: Why do water drops hold together?
answer: Water molecules tug on other water molecules near them. A molecule deep in water is pulled from many directions. A molecule at the surface has much less water above it, so the surface tends to draw tight. This is called surface tension. It helps make a small drop round rather than spread very far. When the conditions are right, a small insect can stand on top of water without breaking through, with its feet making little dents in the surface.

title: How does soap help water wash away grease?
answer: A greasy surface can make plain water form separate drops. Soap changes how these materials meet. Part of a soap molecule gets along with water, while another part gets along with oil. title: Why can soap make a bubble last?
answer: A bubble forms when air stretches a thin liquid film around itself. Water alone usually cannot keep that delicate film from breaking for very long. Soap makes the film easier to stretch and helps it hold together longer. A floating bubble tends toward a round shape because its film pulls toward the smallest surface it can make around that amount of air. title: Why do oil-based dressings sometimes separate?
answer: Oil and vinegar can look like a single cloudy liquid after you shake a dressing. The motion breaks the oil into drops and spreads them through the watery vinegar. A mixture like this is called an emulsion. The drops can eventually come together into a layer again. Some foods use an ingredient that sits where the oil and water meet. title: How can you tell a chemical reaction happened?
answer: A chemical reaction happens when starting substances change into different substances. Their atoms are arranged in new ways. Perhaps you see a new color, see bubbles or feel a temperature change. Those signs can give a clue, but one sign by itself does not prove what happened. Soda can release bubbles that were already dissolved in it. By contrast, when iron rusts, part of the iron becomes a different substance that has a red-brown color and new properties.
facts: Atoms are rearranged during ordinary reactions rather than made from nothing.

title: Why can baking soda make batter rise?
answer: Baking soda can react with a food acid in wet batter and release carbon dioxide gas. The gas makes little bubbles that take up room. In an oven, the batter can set around those bubbles, leaving open spaces and making the baked food feel lighter. If the recipe uses a different source of gas, the spaces can look similar even though the gas formed in a different way. Bread made with yeast can hold carbon dioxide, too.

title: What do pH numbers tell us?
answer: pH is a way to describe how acidic or basic a water-based liquid is. Around room temperature, pure water is neutral and has a pH about 7. Lemon juice and vinegar are on the acidic side, with lower numbers. A liquid with a pH above 7 is on the basic side. Scientists can use an instrument or a substance that changes color to help check the pH. Two clear liquids can have quite different pH values.
facts: Near room temperature, pure water has a pH close to 7.

title: How can a color show whether something is acidic?
answer: Some coloring substances take on different colors in acidic and basic liquids. We call a substance used this way an indicator. A purple color from red cabbage, for instance, can become pinker in an acidic liquid and take on a different color in a basic one. Acidic and basic conditions change the structure of some of its color molecules. A color comparison can give a useful clue about pH, even if both liquids started out clear.

title: Why do some water drops leave white spots?
answer: As rain or groundwater moves through rocks, it can pick up small amounts of minerals. Water with a lot of dissolved calcium or magnesium is called hard water. You usually cannot see those minerals floating in the water. When a drop dries on a faucet or glass, however, some mineral material can stay behind as a pale spot. The spot is a clue that the water was carrying something besides water molecules. Soap may also behave differently in hard water.

title: Why does ice float on liquid water?
answer: In liquid water, molecules can move and slip close to one another. When ordinary ice forms, the molecules lock into a regular arrangement with more open space. The amount of water can stay the same while its solid form takes up more room. That makes ice less dense than liquid water. A piece of ice can float with some of itself above the surface and more of itself below. This is one reason pond ice forms at the top.

facts: The same amount of water takes up more space as ordinary ice than as liquid water.

title: Why does soda fizz when you open it?
answer: A bottle of soda holds carbon dioxide mixed into the liquid. Inside the closed bottle, the gas above the drink pushes on the liquid. This higher pressure helps the liquid hold more dissolved gas. Opening the bottle lowers that pressure. Gas begins to leave the liquid, forming bubbles that rise and pop. Tiny rough places in a glass can give the bubbles places to start. When enough gas has escaped, the drink tastes flatter even though much of the liquid is still there.

facts: Carbon dioxide can remain dissolved in a drink even when you see very few bubbles.

Paint and some other coatings can protect an iron object if they keep air and water from touching the metal. A dry object can stay in better shape for much longer.

A spoon or sink made of stainless steel can stay bright through many washings. Some conditions, such as long contact with salt, can still damage it.

The bread keeps many of the pockets after it bakes, which makes it easier to bite than a solid baked lump of flour and water.

title: Where does vanilla flavor come from?
answer: Vanilla can come from the fruit of a climbing orchid. People often call the long fruit a vanilla bean, even though it is an orchid pod. Its flower must receive pollen to make that pod, and growers in many places pollinate the flowers by hand. The green pods do not start with the same strong scent as finished vanilla. A process of drying and other changes develops the familiar smell used to flavor foods. Small dark seeds can be seen inside some cured pods.
facts: Vanilla pods grow from the flowers of a climbing orchid.

title: How does liquid milk become solid cheese?
answer: In many kinds of cheese making, a change in milk makes its proteins gather to form soft parts called curds. A watery liquid called whey can drain away. The cheese maker can then shape the curds. Choices about what stays inside, how much it is pressed, and whether the cheese is aged help produce cheeses with different textures. A fresh cheese can hold a fair amount of water and feel soft. A cheese that loses more water can become much firmer.
facts: Cheese makers can leave different amounts of water in the curds.

title: Why is yogurt thicker than milk?
answer: In yogurt making, certain helpful bacteria use some of the sugar in milk and produce lactic acid. The acid makes the milk more sour. It also changes how milk proteins fit together, so they can hold water in a soft network. That is why yogurt can stay on a spoon more easily than fresh milk. Some yogurt can release a thin layer of liquid on top if it sits. That layer comes from the mixture giving up a little water.
facts: Yogurt gets some of its tangy flavor from lactic acid.

title: How can cream turn into butter?
answer: Cream contains many small drops of milk fat in a watery liquid. Churning moves the cream around until more of the drops bump together and stick. Eventually, the fat collects in soft pieces. Some watery liquid can drain away. That leaves a material with a much bigger share of milk fat, which is butter. Churning changes the way the parts of cream are arranged. It is different from turning water into ice, because the fat and watery part of the cream end up separated.
facts: The watery part that can drain away during traditional churning is called buttermilk.

title: What does pasteurized mean on a milk carton?
answer: Pasteurizing milk means a dairy heats it for a carefully measured time and then cools it. The process reduces harmful germs so the milk is safer to drink. It does not make regular milk keep forever. People usually still store it cold and use it while fresh. Some drinks made from fruit are pasteurized as well. The process uses heat to make a food safer while keeping much of what people expect from the original food, such as the taste and texture.

title: Why are raisins smaller than grapes?
answer: A grape carries a lot of water inside it. When it is dried into a raisin, much of that water leaves and the skin wrinkles around the smaller fruit. Some of the sugar is still there, but there is less water with it. This can make raisins taste quite sweet in each small bite. Other fruits can also be dried. Drying changes their feel and weight, and it can help them keep longer by taking away water that many little living things need.
facts: A dried fruit can have a stronger sweet taste in the same-sized bite because it has less water.

title: Why does thawed fruit sometimes feel softer?
answer: Inside a piece of fruit, little cells hold water and other materials. When fruit freezes, some of that water becomes ice crystals. Growing ice can damage parts of the cells and the tiny spaces between them. After thawing, juice can leak out more easily and the fruit can feel softer than before it froze. Fast freezing usually leads to smaller crystals, which can cause less damage. A soft thawed berry can still be useful in a food where firmness does not matter much.

facts: Faster freezing often gives ice crystals less time to grow before the fruit freezes through.

title: What makes fruit jam thick enough to spread?
answer: A lot of fruits contain a substance called pectin. Under the right conditions, pectin molecules form a loose network that can hold water. That network gives some fruit spreads a soft, thick texture. Sugar and acid can help certain kinds of pectin form a useful network. Jam often keeps mashed or chopped fruit, while jelly often starts with clear juice. Each can feel thick on a spoon even though much of it is still water.

title: How does a saguaro cactus save water?
answer: A saguaro has a tall, green stem with folds along its sides. It can store water in that stem when rain is available. As more water enters, the folds unfold some, so the stem can get thicker. Many roots stretch sideways just below the surface, where some rain can quickly reach them. A slow-growing saguaro can live through dry stretches using water already inside. Its sharp spines are different from the wide, thin leaves you might see on a garden plant.

title: Why do little maple “helicopters” spin?
answer: Many maples have dry fruits with a thin wing around or beside a pocket holding a seed. When a fruit falls, the wing can make it turn in the air. The turning slows its trip to the ground. A breeze gets more time to push it sideways, so the seed may land farther from the parent tree. Two fruits often start joined in a pair before they separate. The little “helicopter” you find already carries everything enclosed with that seed.
facts: A winged maple fruit is called a samara.

title: What can grow from a white oak acorn?
answer: A white oak grows acorns, the hard nuts found under the tree. Much of an acorn gives food and protection to its seed while it waits. Some animals eat acorns right away. Squirrels and jays can also carry them to save for later. An acorn that stays hidden in damp ground may send down a root and grow into a young oak. facts: White oak acorns usually begin sending out a root soon after they fall if conditions are suitable.

title: Do sunflowers turn to follow the Sun?
answer: A young sunflower may face east in the morning and turn westward by late afternoon. One side of its stem grows faster than the other at different times, bending the plant as it grows. The movement follows a daily rhythm. Once the stem grows more slowly and the flower head matures, the head often stays facing east rather than turning all day. Early sunlight can warm the head, giving it a head start when insects begin visiting after sunrise.

title: Why is bamboo a grass when it looks like a tree?
answer: Bamboo can grow tall, hard stems that look almost like small tree trunks. It is still in the grass family, along with lawn grass, wheat and rice. Many bamboo stems have hollow places between solid or stronger joints. A bamboo patch can put up shoots from stems that spread below ground. title: Why do water drops roll off a lotus leaf?
answer: A lotus leaf can look smooth from a distance. Up close, its surface has tiny bumps and a waxy coating. A drop of water touches only a small part of that surface, so it often rests as a round bead rather than spreading out like a puddle. As a drop rolls, it can pick up loose dirt. The shape of the leaf’s surface and the way water pulls on itself both help explain why a lotus leaf can stay cleaner after rain.
facts: A rolling drop can carry particles of dust away from a lotus leaf.

title: Why does garlic come apart into cloves?
answer: The round piece of garlic in a kitchen is a bulb. Peel away its dry outer covering and you can see several smaller pieces called cloves. answer: The familiar part of a carrot is a thick main root. It can hold food the plant made earlier in its green leaves. title: Why do shoots sometimes bend toward a window?
answer: A young stem beside a window can bend as it grows. The side away from the strongest light can stretch more than the lit side. With one side getting longer, the whole stem curves toward the window. Bending as it grows can put its leaves where they catch more light. Scientists call this response phototropism. Growth can change again if the main source of light moves. The shoot does not turn by moving a joint in the way you turn an elbow.
facts: The same amount of light from different directions can change how a shoot bends.

title: How does a root know which way is down?
answer: A root does not need to see the ground to grow down into it. Certain cells near many root tips can detect the direction of gravity. Signals from those cells affect how much parts of the root grow. If a seed is turned sideways, a new root can soon curve downward. Stems often respond by bending upward. The growth pattern is called gravitropism. It helps a seed get some roots into the ground and some shoots toward open space where leaves can catch light.
facts: Shoots and many roots can respond in opposite directions to gravity.

title: Why does water bubble when it boils?
answer: As water heats, more of its molecules can move into a gas. At the boiling point, bubbles of water vapor can grow inside the liquid and reach the surface. Evaporation can happen just at the surface long before a pot boils. Air pressure around the water helps set its boiling point. Higher on a mountain, the pressure is lower, so water generally begins boiling at a lower temperature. Bubbling water can therefore be at different temperatures in different places.

title: Why does plywood have layers that face different ways?
answer: A piece of solid wood often splits more easily in the direction its fibers run. In plywood, a panel is made by gluing together thin sheets of wood. The grain of one sheet often runs across the grain of the next one. That can keep the whole panel from having one easy direction to split. It can also help the sheet stay flatter when moisture changes. Looking at a plywood edge may show several thin lines where the different sheets meet.
facts: A thin sheet of wood used as a layer is called veneer.

title: Why does a wool sweater help keep you warm?
answer: Wool comes from the coat of an animal, often a sheep. Its fine fibers often have little bends or waves. When the fibers are made into yarn and fabric, they can trap small spaces filled with air. Air that stays mostly still can slow the movement of heat away from your body. title: What part of a flax plant becomes linen?

facts: Linen fibers grow along the flax stem, not on the outside of a seed.
